process_name: Cloud Cost Anomaly Detection and Remediation
overview: This process identifies and resolves unexpected increases in cloud spend across hybrid environments (AWS, on-premise, SaaS platforms). It is triggered when a cost anomaly is detected via monitoring or billing data. The process correlates cost signals with infrastructure changes, utilisation metrics, and observability data (logs, metrics, traces) to determine root cause. The system then generates recommended actions to reduce cost and routes these actions to the appropriate teams for approval and execution via ITSM workflows.
key_steps: Detect cost anomaly via billing or monitoring signal
Correlate cost signal with infrastructure changes and deployment history
Correlate with observability data (logs, metrics, traces from Splunk/New Relic)
Identify top cost drivers (service, team, resource type)
Classify issue type (right-sizing, idle resource, verbosity, pricing model)
Rank actions by cost saving potential and risk
Route actions to responsible team owners
Create ServiceNow tickets for approved actions
Request approvals from FinOps and Application Teams
Close tickets and update cost baseline
pain_points: Fragmented tooling across AWS billing, Splunk, New Relic, and ServiceNow
Slow manual analysis taking hours to days to identify root cause
Poor visibility into which team or application owns anomalous spend
High observability platform cost driven by excessive log verbosity
Inconsistent remediation practices across application teams
Approval bottlenecks slowing execution of time-sensitive optimizations
No closed-loop validation that remediation actions achieved expected savings
automation_goals: Automated closed-loop detect → analyse → act → validate cycle
AI-driven root cause analysis correlating multiple data sources
Automated ticket creation and routing in ServiceNow
Intelligent approval routing based on action risk and cost threshold
Automated execution of low-risk remediation actions
Continuous validation and cost baseline updates
approvals: FinOps approval required for any action with cost impact > $1,000/month
Application Team owner approval required before executing changes in their environment
Cloud Platform Engineering approval required for infrastructure-level changes
risks: False positive anomaly detection causing unnecessary remediation
Automated execution of actions in wrong environment
Approval delays exceeding SLA for time-sensitive cost spikes
Insufficient tagging/ownership metadata causing routing failures
constraints: Must integrate with existing ServiceNow ITSM workflows
Cannot modify production infrastructure without approved change ticket
Must comply with data residency requirements
Observability data access governed by existing Splunk/New Relic access controls
success_metrics: Mean time to detect anomaly < 15 minutes
Mean time to remediate < 4 hours for automated actions
Percentage of anomalies with automated root cause identification > 80%
